description: AI model-development startup building open-weight coding models (the Laguna family) via its internal "Model Factory." NVIDIA struck a non-exclusive $6B licensing deal for that technology and separately invested $1B in a growth round at a $12-13B valuation, while extending offers to over 100 Poolside researchers.

Moraga, California startup (keplercompute.com) developing AI memory/logic chips using 3D-stacked ferroelectric architecture that puts compute next to weight storage, aimed at easing the von Neumann bottleneck. Signed a Commerce Dept. CHIPS Act letter of intent for up to $245M R&D funding (part of an $874M, 7-company tranche), with the government taking a minority equity stake. Note: batch context cites $490M; public reporting on this LOI states $245M for Kepler specifically.

ETH Zurich spinout (founded 2022, ~75 people) building the "Gravis Rack," a hardware-agnostic retrofit system that makes existing excavators and heavy construction equipment (Caterpillar, John Deere, JCB, Hitachi, Volvo) autonomous. Raised a $200M Series A solely from SoftBank on Aug 17, 2026 — the largest in construction-robotics history — valuing it at $1B.

Publicly traded (Nasdaq: ALMU) semiconductor company developing non-InP substrate photonics for high-speed datacom, quantum, and AI-interconnect applications. Signed a Dept. of Commerce CHIPS R&D Office letter of intent on July 29, 2026 for up to $30M to scale domestic manufacturing of photodetectors and lasers for next-gen AI networking; award still subject to due diligence and definitive documents.

Toronto "world model" startup founded in 2026 by ex-NVIDIA researcher Sanja Fidler with Huan Ling and Zan Gojcic, building multimodal foundation models that simulate physical reality to train embodied/robotics AI. Raised a $90M+ seed co-led by Khosla Ventures and Radical Ventures on Aug 19, 2026 — one of the largest Canadian seed rounds ever, just three months after founding.

New York holding company spun out of Thrive Capital (Josh Kushner) that acquires legacy services businesses — accounting (Current, 50+ firms) and IT (Shield, ~20 firms) — and embeds AI into their operations; OpenAI took an equity stake in December 2025. Raised $2B at a $12B valuation on Aug 12, 2026 from Altimeter Capital, D1 Capital Partners and SoftBank.

AI-native accounting/ERP platform serving 600+ finance teams. Raised a $100M Series C led by ICONIQ with Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz participating (Aug 19, 2026), hitting unicorn status at a $1B valuation two years after emerging from stealth; prior rounds were a $25M Series A (Sequoia) and $70M Series B (ICONIQ/a16z).

target: Paducah DOE Site AI Data Center Campus
description: A roughly $100B AI data-center campus planned on the DOE's Paducah, Kentucky site (a former uranium-enrichment plant), developed and operated by Brookfield with NextEra Energy building dedicated gas and battery generation (up to 4.6GW). Announced July 29, 2026; targets up to 1.2GW of compute load by 2032, with first components online as early as 2028.

Biotech-AI startup founded 2022 (Asad Ali Ahmad, Raphael Potter) built on a research network of academic biobanks (Mass General Brigham, UPenn, CU Anschutz) providing the world's largest patient tissue/blood/clinical training dataset for disease-specific AI models, plus an NVIDIA collaboration on a cell-free-RNA foundation model. Launched publicly Aug 19, 2026 with $50M from Founders Fund, Section 32, Thiel Bio, Breyer Capital and others.

target: NVIDIA AI Compute Infrastructure Financing Platform
description: Not a company but a set of MOU-based financing platforms NVIDIA is establishing with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize over $500B of third-party capital for AI-compute/datacenter buildout across NVIDIA's customer ecosystem (frontier labs, enterprises, neoclouds). Announced Aug 10, 2026; MOUs signed, no capital deployed under the framework yet.

Los Angeles startup founded by three former SpaceX Starlink laser-comms engineers (Travis Brashears, Cameron Ramos, Serena Grown-Haeberli) building optical transceivers (Alpha C1, 1.6Tbps) linking GPUs across AI datacenters at lower power than copper. Raised a $50M Series A led by Thrive Capital in Feb 2026; Elon Musk personally got FTC clearance to acquire the company on June 25, 2026 (terms undisclosed).

Vinod Khosla's venture firm is in talks to raise a record $5.5B across a new set of funds (~$1B seed, $2B early-stage, $2.5B growth) — its largest fundraise ever, reflecting heavy AI conviction (early OpenAI, Cognition, Sakana AI backer). Reported by Bloomberg July 23, 2026; talks were private and fund sizes/names not yet finalized.

Defense-tech startup developing Blackbeard, a low-cost mass-producible hypersonic strike missile (program of record, fielding targeted 2027), with $500M+ in US military contracts over 18 months. Raised a $1B Series C ($800M equity + $250M credit facility) on Aug 19, 2026, co-led by J.P. Morgan's Strategic Investment Group, Andreessen Horowitz and Carlyle, with Altimeter, Lightspeed and General Catalyst participating; values Castelion at $13B.

target: Akita AI Data Center (BitGrid / S2 JV)
description: A planned ~2 trillion yen (~$12.6B), up to 500MW AI data-center project in Akita, Japan, via a joint special-purpose company formed by US startup Bitgrit and local firm S2 (first MOU with Akita city, Oct 2025); a smaller 1.5MW facility is targeted for late 2027. UAE sovereign fund Mubadala (via MGX) is reportedly weighing an investment of up to ~$6.3-6.8B. Note: batch spells the partner "BitGrid"; press coverage consistently spells it "Bitgrit" — likely the same entity, spelling unconfirmed.
